title: How to Tell if a Peptide Vendor Is Legit: {n} Checks
Is a Peptide Vendor Legit? {n} Checks
description: How to tell if a peptide vendor is legit: {n} checks with real cases from our audit of {shops} shops, from cropped lab reports to missing company data.
How to tell if a peptide vendor is legit: {n} checks with real cases from our audit of {shops} shops.
lg.h1: How to tell if a peptide vendor is legit
lg.intro: Check {n} things before you trust a shop: can the lab report be opened on the lab's own portal, is it complete, does the shop copy match, do the batch numbers fit, where is it hosted, and is there a company behind it. Each check below comes with a real case from our audit of {shops} shops on {date}.
lg.statsP: Out of {shops} shops: {noRep} published no report we could open, {noPortal} had no report we could confirm on a lab portal, and {noEntity} publish no company name.
lg.fq1: How can I tell if a peptide company is legit?
lg.fa1: Open its lab report and look for the same report on the testing lab's own website, check that batch numbers and sizes match the product, and look for a named company with an address. {portal} of the {reports} reports we opened could be confirmed this way.
lg.fq2: Is a COA proof that a peptide vendor is legit?
lg.fa2: Not on its own. We found cropped report images, shop copies missing a line that the lab's copy shows, batch labels that do not match and reports stored only on Google Drive. A report counts only if the lab's portal confirms it.
lg.fq3: What are the red flags of a fake peptide vendor?
lg.fa3: No public lab reports or reports only on request, reports that cannot be found on the lab portal, cropped or edited images, batch numbers that are missing or do not match, and no company name or address.
lg.fq4: Where can I check a peptide vendor's lab report?
lg.fa4: On the testing lab's own website, using the report number or key printed on the report. Our lab guides explain the steps for each lab.
lg.relJanoshik: How to verify a Janoshik report

portal.h: Can the report be opened on the lab's own portal?
portal.why: A shop can upload any file. Only the lab's own website shows what the lab really issued.
portal.how: Type the report number or key into the lab's verification page and compare every line.

cropped.h: Is the whole report shown, not cropped?
cropped.why: A cropped image hides the task number, client and batch, so nobody can match it to a product.
cropped.how: Look for the full page: lab name, task number, client, batch, test date and the verification key.

copy.h: Does the shop's copy match the lab's copy?
copy.why: If the shop's PDF lacks a line that the lab's copy has, the shop has edited or replaced the file.
copy.how: Download both copies of the same report ID and compare them line by line.

batch.h: Do batch numbers and sample names fit the product?
batch.why: A report for a different size or batch says nothing about the vial you would receive.
batch.how: Compare the sample name, size and batch on the report with the product page.

drive.why: Files on Google Drive or the shop's own server can be changed at any time and carry no proof of origin.
drive.how: Prefer reports you can open on the lab's portal over files in cloud folders.

nobatch.h: Does the report carry a batch number at all?
nobatch.why: Without a batch number a report cannot be linked to any lot on sale.
nobatch.how: Check that the batch or lot field is filled in, not blank, "N/A" or "Unknown".

entity.h: Is there a company behind the shop?
entity.why: Without a company name and address you do not know who is responsible.
entity.how: Look for a legal name, address and registration number in the terms, imprint or contact page.

onrequest.h: Are lab reports public, or only on request?
onrequest.why: Testing claims you cannot read cannot be checked.
onrequest.how: Count "COA on request" as no public report until you can open it on the lab's portal.

title: Is It Legal to Buy Peptides Online? ({year})
Is It Legal to Buy Peptides Online?
description: Is it legal to buy peptides online? What the FDA says about research-use-only peptides, plus medicines rules for {n} countries, with sources. General information.
Is it legal to buy peptides online? What the FDA says about research-use-only peptides, plus rules for {n} countries.
leg.h1: Is it legal to buy peptides online?
leg.intro: It depends on the country and on how the product is sold. Research peptides are sold as laboratory reagents for research use only. FDA warning letters say this label does not decide the matter: when a website shows products are meant for people, the FDA classes them as unapproved new drugs. In Europe, national medicines laws apply.
leg.usH: United States: what the FDA says
leg.us1: The FDA says it has warned companies that sold unapproved drugs containing semaglutide, tirzepatide, retatrutide, survodutide or mazdutide labelled "for research purposes" or "not for human consumption", and urges consumers not to buy these products.
leg.us2: The FDA says retatrutide and cagrilintide cannot be used in compounding under federal law and are not components of any FDA-approved drug.
leg.us3: In its warning letters the FDA states that a research-use-only label did not stop it from classing the products as unapproved new drugs, because the sellers' websites showed they were intended for people.
leg.lettersH: Recent FDA warning letters to peptide sellers
leg.euP: Outside the US, medicines are regulated by national law. Our country notes name the authority and the main law for {n} countries:
leg.ourP: We compare prices and lab data of products sold as laboratory reagents for research use only. We do not give advice on importing, customs or personal use, and nothing here is a recommendation to buy a product for use in people.
leg.fq1: Are peptides legal in the US?
leg.fa1: Some peptides are approved medicines available on prescription. Unapproved peptides sold for human use are, according to the FDA, unapproved new drugs, and a "research use only" label does not change that when products are marketed for people.
leg.fq2: Does a "research use only" label make a purchase legal?
leg.fa2: No label settles it. The FDA judges how a product is actually marketed. In its warning letters it classed research-labelled semaglutide, tirzepatide and retatrutide as unapproved new drugs.
leg.fq3: Are research peptides legal in Europe?
leg.fa3: Each country applies its own medicines law, for example the Arzneimittelgesetz in Germany or the Public Health Code in France. Our country notes list the authority and the main law for {n} countries.
leg.fa4: Retatrutide is an investigational Eli Lilly molecule that has not been approved by the FDA or any other regulator. Lilly says products claiming to be retatrutide offered to consumers are unlawful.
leg.relReta: Can you buy retatrutide in the USA?
leg.relLegit: How to tell if a vendor is legit

ret.h1: Can you buy retatrutide in the USA?
ret.intro: Not as an approved medicine. Retatrutide is an investigational Eli Lilly molecule in Phase 3 trials and has not been approved by the FDA or any other regulator. The FDA says it cannot be used in compounding, and Lilly says any product claiming to be retatrutide offered to consumers is unlawful.
ret.vStatus: Investigational molecule (Eli Lilly), Phase 3; not approved by the FDA or any other regulator.

ret.lettersP: These letters went to sellers that offered retatrutide under its own name or a code name. The FDA classed the products as unapproved new drugs despite "research use only" labels.
ret.ruoP: Some shops list retatrutide as a laboratory reagent, often under code names such as GLP-3 RT or RT-3. Our price comparison shows these research listings with lab data. A listing does not make a product legal for any particular use, and nothing on this site is a recommendation to buy it for use in people.
ret.dataP: In our audit, {n} of {shops} shops listed retatrutide ({eu} in Europe, {us} in the USA), and we opened {reports} retatrutide lab reports.
ret.fa1: No. Lilly says retatrutide has not been approved by the FDA or any other regulatory authority and remains an investigational molecule.
ret.fa2: No. The FDA says retatrutide cannot be used in compounding under federal law.
ret.fq3: Is research-use-only retatrutide legal in the USA?

title: Peptide COA Red Flags: {n} Real Cases We Found
Peptide COA Red Flags: Real Cases
description: Peptide COA red flags: {n} real cases from our audit, from cropped or edited reports to batch mismatches, plus {out} reports outside 90–110 % of label.
Peptide COA red flags: {n} real cases from our audit of {shops} shops, with sources.
rf.h1: Peptide COA red flags: what we found in real reports
rf.intro: A certificate of analysis is only useful if it is complete, matches the product and can be confirmed by the lab. Below are {n} red flags we found while opening {reports} reports from {shops} shops on {date}, each with the shop and the source, plus every report whose measured content was outside 90–110 % of the label.
rf.outH: Reports with measured content outside 90–110 % of the label
rf.outP: {out} of {withFill} reports with a measured amount were outside this band ({low} below, {high} above). Above-label results are common and not a quality problem in themselves, but they show that the label alone tells you little.
rf.fq1: What are red flags on a peptide COA?
rf.fa1: A cropped or edited image, no task number or verification key, a missing or mismatched batch number, a sample name or size that does not match the product, a shop copy that differs from the lab's copy, and a report that cannot be found on the lab's portal.
rf.fq2: How can I tell if a COA is fake?
rf.fa2: Enter the task number and key on the lab's own website and compare every line with the shop's copy. Of the {reports} reports we opened, {portal} could be confirmed this way.
rf.fq3: Is a higher measured amount than the label a red flag?
rf.fa3: Not necessarily. {high} of {withFill} measured reports we opened were above 110 % of the label and {low} were below 90 %. Large swings in both directions show the label alone is not a reliable guide.
rf.fq4: Can a real COA belong to a different batch?
rf.fa4: Yes. A genuine report for another batch or vial size says nothing about the vial on sale. Check that sample name, size and batch match the product page.
rf.relRead: How to read a peptide COA

title: How to Read a Peptide COA: Annotated Example
How to Read a Peptide COA
description: How to read a peptide COA: an annotated sample report, what each field means, purity vs measured mg, and the red flags we found in {reports} real reports.
How to read a peptide COA: annotated sample report, field by field, with red flags from {reports} reports.
coa.h1: How to read a peptide COA (certificate of analysis)
coa.intro: A peptide COA is a lab report for one sample. Read it in this order: who tested it (lab, task number, key), what was tested (sample name, batch, client), how (method, for example HPLC) and what came out (purity and measured mg). Then confirm the same report on the lab's own portal: {portal} of the {reports} reports we opened could be confirmed that way.
coa.figNote: Our own drawing with placeholder values. It is not a copy of any real report.

f1.p: The lab that ran the test. Look it up yourself instead of following a link on the shop's site.

f2.p: The lab's own ID for this test. You need it to find the report on the lab's portal.

f3.p: A second code that unlocks the lab's record. Without it many portals cannot show the report.

f4.p: Who sent the sample. It may be the shop, a manufacturer or a third party; a blank client field is worth asking about.

f5.p: What the sample was declared as, for example a 10 mg vial. It must match the product you are looking at.

f6.p: Links the report to one production lot. Blank, "N/A" or "Unknown" means it cannot be tied to any vial on sale.

f7.p: When the sample was analysed. An old date may belong to an earlier lot.

f8.p: How the result was measured. HPLC gives purity and amount; mass spectrometry (MS) confirms identity.

f9.p: The share of the target peptide in the sample by HPLC. In the reports we opened it ranged from {pmin} to {pmax}.

f10.p: How many mg the lab found in the vial, compared with the label. {within} of {withFill} measured reports we opened were within 90–110 % of the label.

coa.pvH: Purity and content are two different numbers
coa.pvP: Purity says how clean the peptide is; content says how much of it is in the vial. A vial can be 99 % pure and still hold less or more than the label states. Price per mg only makes sense with the measured content in mind.
coa.distTitle: Measured content vs label in the reports we opened
coa.panelsH: What a COA usually does not cover
coa.panelsP: Most reports test purity and amount only. Of {shops} shops, {endo} list endotoxin testing, {ster} sterility testing, {metals} heavy metals and {ms} an LC-MS identity test.
coa.redP: Cropped images, missing batch numbers, shop copies that differ from the lab's copy and reports that cannot be found on the portal. We list real cases with sources on a separate page.
coa.checkLink: Check a report number in our data
coa.fq1: What is a COA for peptides?
coa.fa1: A certificate of analysis is a lab report for one sample of a peptide: identity, purity and usually the measured amount per vial, with the lab's task number and a verification key.
coa.fq2: What does HPLC purity mean on a COA?
coa.fa2: It is the share of the target peptide among everything the HPLC detected in the sample, given in percent. In the {reports} reports we opened it ranged from {pmin} to {pmax}.
coa.fq3: How do I verify a peptide COA?
coa.fa3: Type the lab's address into your browser yourself, open its verification page and enter the task number and key from the report. Compare compound, amount, purity, batch and date with the shop's copy.
coa.fq4: Why does the measured mg differ from the label?
coa.fa4: Filling is never exact, and labs measure what is actually in the vial. Of {withFill} measured reports we opened, {low} were below 90 % of the label and {high} above 110 %.
coa.fq5: Does a COA show endotoxin or sterility?
coa.fa5: Only if those tests were ordered. Most reports we opened cover purity and amount only; {endo} of {shops} shops list endotoxin testing.
